newsitem.title: THAILAND: Liquor sales up as Thais beat pre-poll booze ban.
newsitem.headline: Liquor sales up as Thais beat pre-poll booze ban.

text.p: Sales of liquor were brisk on Saturday as Thailand prepared to ban the sale and consumption of alchohol in public ahead of Sunday's general election, grocers and shopkeepers reported.
The ban, required by law to ensure an orderly election, would go into effect from 6 p.m. on Saturday until 6 a.m. on Monday, election commission officials told Reuters.
Offenders face jail terms of one to five years or a fine of up to 50,000 Baht ($2,000), they said. In the July 1995 election, 58 people were prosecuted for the offence.
Most election canvassers and politicians had already stocked their bars to tide them over the polling period into the early hours of Monday morning, their aides said.
Thousands of tourists visiting Thailand during the weekend will be affected by the ban.
"The law only bans people from drinking in public but they can still drink in their houses," an election commission official said, adding that foreign tourists could drinks in their hotel rooms.
A total of 38 million voters are set to cast their votes on Sunday in the polls.
